subject: Re: Order Form — commit tranches, invoice schedule & tax certificates
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Finance <finance@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-20 11:02 -0700
Subject: Order Form: Redwood – initial redlines on commercials

Hi Sean,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Please find attached our commercial redlines (Acme_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx) and our VAT registration certificate. High-level points from procurement and finance: 

- Commit tranching: we want the committed usage to be split into three tranches (Q3, Q4, Q1) tied to delivery milestones rather than a single upfront min commit.
- Pricing ladder: requests to add a stepped volume discount at 250K/500K token thresholds; need clarity how overage pricing applies between tiers.
- Invoicing cadence: finance prefers milestone invoices aligned to tranches; proposed Net 60 payment terms for milestone invoices.
- Taxes: Acme is VAT-registered in the EU; we will provide VAT certificates but need Redwood to accept reverse-charge where applicable. If Redwood needs to charge VAT, please confirm tax handling/responsibility.
- PO requirements: every invoice must include the Acme PO number and a specific PO prefix (ACME-2027-).

Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility on tranching + Net 60? Also, can legal/finance at Redwood advise whether the VAT certificate acceptance window (we propose 30 days) is acceptable contractually?

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx (25 KB); VAT_Registration_Acme.pdf (80 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20 13:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Redwood – initial redlines on commercials

Lina — thanks for the redlines and the VAT certificate. Appreciated. 

Quick summary of next steps from our side: 
- Commercial flexibility: we can support a tranche-based minimum commit (Q3/Q4/Q1) but we need an agreed ladder that pins the committed token volumes per tranche and a fallback clause if a tranche is not consumed.
- Net terms / invoicing: we typically operate Net 30 but are open to milestone Net 60 for large enterprise deals if there is an upfront non-refundable booking (we would propose 25% of the first tranche up front). The other option is Net 30 with a 2% early-pay discount if you can move payments sooner.
- Taxes: we can accept VAT certificates for reverse-charge but legal will need the certificate before we mark invoices VAT-free. We also require a contractual clause stating Redwood's right to charge taxes retroactively if a certificate is invalid.
- PO prefix and numbering: happy to include the ACME-2027- prefix in our invoice number field — we'll show both Redwood invoice # and Acme PO on the PDF.

I've looped in Monica (finance) and Karthik (legal) to propose specific contract language and a sample invoice template. Attaching a sample invoice for format reference.

Can you confirm whether Acme is agreeable to either: (A) 25% upfront + milestone Net 60, or (B) Net 30 + 2% within 15 days? Once you pick, we will generate a redlined order form for signature.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_invoice_sample.pdf (5 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21 09:30 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form: Redwood – proposed contractual language for tranches/invoicing/tax

Lina / Sean — taking a pass from legal. Quoting your key asks and proposing contractual language below.

On 20 Jun 2027, 11:02, Lina Torres wrote:
> - Commit tranching: split into three tranches tied to milestones
> - Net 60 for milestone invoices
> - VAT certificates provided; Redwood to accept reverse-charge where valid

Proposed redline snippets we can include in the Order Form (high level):

1) Commit Tranches and Fallback: 
"Customer shall commit to the Token Volumes set forth in the Order Form by tranche (Tranche 1, Tranche 2, Tranche 3). If Customer fails to consume at least 80% of any tranche by the tranche end date, Redwood may (a) allow crediting of unconsumed tokens to subsequent tranches within 90 days, or (b) invoice 50% of the unconsumed tranche amount as a breakup fee, at Redwood's election. 

2) Invoicing and Payment Terms: 
"Invoices for each tranche milestone will be issued upon milestone acceptance. Standard payment terms are Net 30. For this Order Form, the parties agree to Net 60 for milestone invoices, subject to Customer providing a non-refundable initial booking payment equal to 25% of Tranche 1 within 10 days of Order Form execution. Redwood will provide an invoice that includes both the Redwood invoice number and Customer PO. Early-pay discount (2%) applies if Customer pays within 15 days, unless the parties opt for early-pay discount to be voided in exchange for Net 60 without initial booking payment."

3) Taxes and Certificates: 
"Customer shall provide valid VAT/tax registration certificates within 30 days of Order Form execution. If Customer provides a valid certificate and reverse-charge applies under applicable law, Redwood will not charge VAT. If no valid certificate is provided within 30 days, or if Customer later withdraws or invalidates such certificate, Redwood reserves the right to (i) charge applicable taxes on past and future invoices, and (ii) seek reimbursement for taxes, penalties, or interest from Customer on a retroactive basis."

4) PO and Invoice Numbering: 
"All invoices shall reference the Customer PO number. Customer may request a PO prefix; Redwood will include the prefix in its invoice numbering and metadata."

We're also attaching a draft Order Form amendment that incorporates these snippets for your legal review. If Acme can confirm acceptance of the 25% initial booking (or your preference for Net 30 + 2% early-pay), we will incorporate the final redline and circulate for signature.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_Amend_v1.docx (12 KB)

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@acme.com>, Acme Finance <finance@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-22 15:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — commit tranches, invoice schedule & tax certificates

Thanks Karthik and Sean — the language looks good and addresses our main concerns. A few quick points: 

- Acme accepts the tranche structure and fallback credit option (a) in principle. We will provide suggested tranche volumes in a follow-up attachment by EOD tomorrow.
- Acme can provide the VAT certificate within 5 business days. We confirm we expect reverse-charge to apply for the EU entity; we will notify you immediately if anything changes.
- Regarding payment: Acme prefers option (A) (25% upfront + milestone Net 60) — finance has greenlit the booking payment but would like an explicit milestone acceptance definition in the SOW so we can justify milestone invoicing.
- PO prefix: confirmed — invoices should include ACME-2027- as the PO prefix.

If everything above is acceptable, please send the final redline and DocuSign envelope. We will execute promptly once the amendment includes milestone acceptance criteria.

Lina Torres
Sr. Procurement Manager | Acme Corporation

Links: DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/RED-ACME-OrderForm)
Attachments: (will send tranche volumes and SOW acceptance criteria in follow-up)
